body.en:
Question B-003-003-001.

Why the correct answer is right: The radio frequency (RF) amplifier is the receiver front end because it is the first active stage handling the incoming signal from the antenna path.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "Local oscillator": The local oscillator helps tune and mix, but it is not the front-end signal amplifier connected to the incoming RF path.
- sourceIndex 2: "AF amplifier": The AF amplifier is late in the receiver after detection, so it is not the front end.
- sourceIndex 3: "Limiter": A limiter is an FM IF/detector-chain block, not the first RF stage.
